info.title: Section 19 Compliance, Safety and Proof
info.description: Authoritative machine-readable contract. All routes are tenant scoped and deny by default.

CommandRequest.description: Operation-specific JSON request. Unknown fields are rejected by the HTTP decoder where the operation uses a strict DTO.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Expected aggregate version; expectedVersion in the JSON body is also accepted.

post.description: reported -> triaged. Requires severity, location, affected people/asset reference arrays and the immediate actions taken. Emits incident.triaged.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Expected aggregate version; expectedVersion in the JSON body is also accepted.

post.description: triaged -> contained. Requires containmentSummary. Emits incident.contained.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Expected aggregate version; expectedVersion in the JSON body is also accepted.

post.description: reported|triaged|contained|under_investigation|corrective_action -> escalated. Requires trigger (SEVERITY, REGULATORY, CUSTOMER, SAFETY_CRITICAL, OTHER) and reason; the incident later continues from the stage it escalated from. Emits incident.escalated.

get.description: The organization's own investigations of one incident.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Expected aggregate version; expectedVersion in the JSON body is also accepted.

post.description: contained -> under_investigation. Assigns an active organization member as investigator with a scope and an evidence preservation plan. One open investigation per incident. Emits incident.investigation_started.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Expected aggregate version; expectedVersion in the JSON body is also accepted.

post.description: Findings and root cause, submitted by the assigned investigator only.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Expected aggregate version; expectedVersion in the JSON body is also accepted.

post.description: under_investigation -> corrective_action. Approves submitted findings (approver must not be the investigator) and creates the correctiveActions in the same transaction. Emits incident.corrective_action_started.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Expected aggregate version; expectedVersion in the JSON body is also accepted.

post.description: corrective_action -> resolved once every corrective action is verified or cancelled. Emits incident.resolved.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Expected aggregate version; expectedVersion in the JSON body is also accepted.

post.description: resolved -> closed once linked claims are settled, rejected, closed or cancelled. Emits incident.closed.

get.description: Immutable proof record with its append-only verification history and effective status.

post.description: Verifies a proof record against the policy snapshot it was submitted under. The submitter cannot verify their own proof; an organization decision is final. Emits proof.verified.
Rejects a proof record with reasonCodes. A correction is a new superseding proof record. Emits proof.rejected.

get.description: Compliance checks, newest first, filterable by subjectType and subjectReference.

post.description: Evaluates every active requirement of the subject in one transaction and records the check; the strictest result governs. Blocking failures apply restrictions that are propagated to the execution services. Emits compliance_check.completed.

get.description: One immutable compliance check with the evaluations it produced.
